sections.content: How many people stayed in Clifton (City of Nottingham) after gaining qualifications?

Clifton (City of Nottingham) is a medium-sized town in the East Midlands. Clifton (City of Nottingham) does not have its own university.

Clifton (City of Nottingham) has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Clifton (City of Nottingham) ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,150 state-school pupils from Clifton (City of Nottingham) who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 175 (15%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 335 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Clifton (City of Nottingham) to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Clifton (City of Nottingham)'s pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Clifton (City of Nottingham) in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Clifton (City of Nottingham) move to?

Of Clifton (City of Nottingham)'s graduates, 60 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 30 of those graduates (50%) were living fairly locally, in the Nottingham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Clifton (City of Nottingham)'s qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 110 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 85 of those qualified non-graduates (77%) were living fairly locally, in the Nottingham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Clifton (City of Nottingham)'s GCSE cohort:

  • 25 graduates left the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 49% of graduates and 34% of qualified non-graduates living in Clifton (City of Nottingham) had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 225 graduates and 325 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Clifton (City of Nottingham). This is compared with the 175 graduates and 335 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 51% of the graduates had also lived in Clifton (City of Nottingham) as GCSE pupils, while 49% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Clifton (City of Nottingham) in 2018 to 2019, 66% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 34% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
